definition: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that learns small low-rank updates instead of full weight matrices.
details: LoRA freezes the original weights and adds a small trainable low-rank decomposition to each of them, cutting trainable parameters by orders of magnitude. It dramatically reduces the memory and storage needed to adapt a model and allows many lightweight task-specific adapters to be swapped onto one base model.

explainer.lead: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that learns small low-rank updates instead of full weight matrices. It matters because it slashes the memory and storage needed to adapt a model and lets many lightweight adapters share one base.

tiers.eli5: You keep the original recipe and write a short margin note that adjusts it for one occasion, instead of rewriting the whole cookbook.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers freeze the original weights and train low-rank decompositions, then swap task-specific adapters onto a single base model; a pitfall is managing many adapters whose compatibility must be tracked.
tiers.paperLevel: Original weights are frozen; a small trainable low-rank decomposition is added to each, cutting trainable parameters by orders of magnitude.

explainer.example: A base model serves ten customer domains by swapping in a different small adapter for each, all stored on one shared foundation.

citation.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
